subtitle: Create an item by writing its content, without a book image; students can solve it comfortably on a phone.
loadError: The activity could not be loaded.
startedWarning: {{count}} students have started this activity. A new item is shown only to students who start from now on; students who started or finished keep their list.
kindLocked: A saved item’s type can’t be changed; add a new item for another type.

kindHints.matrix: Mark the correct option for each row. The T/F template sets up two columns; with multiple choice a row can have several correct options.
kindHints.classify: Sort the cards into groups. A card that belongs to no group is a distractor.
kindHints.order: Write the items in the correct order; students get them shuffled.
kindHints.match: Write the pairs; distractor right items are optional. Students get the right side shuffled.
kindHints.fillText: Write the text and put [[answer]] where the blank goes. Numeric answers (3/4, 2 1/2, 0.75) become number boxes; others are compared as text (case and trailing punctuation ignored).
kindHints.shortAnswer: Write a question and its accepted answer on each row. Separate several answers with |.
kindHints.fillTable: Fill in the table; write [[answer]] in the cells the student completes. Other cells are shown as is.
kindHints.wordPool: Write the text and wrap the missing word in [[word]]. Words appear shuffled in the bank; you can add distractors.
kindHints.mazeTree: The student picks T or F at each statement and reaches an exit. Mark the answer of every statement; the correct exit follows from them.
kindHints.mazeBoard: Each row has one correct box; the student steps on boxes from bottom to top to reach the finish. A wrong box breaks.
kindHints.mazeRooms: Each room is a question and the doors between rooms are answers. The student follows the correct doors from the start room to the finish.
kindHints.mazeStones: The student crosses by tapping only the «Step» stones; stepping on a «Do not step» stone or skipping a «Step» stone counts as wrong. Switch the stones that must not be stepped on (e.g. false statements) to «Do not step».
kindHints.regionPaint: The student paints each colour in the requested share of an equal-square grid; positions are free, the count per colour is checked.
kindHints.numberLine: Students put the cards (fractions, decimals, events…) on the right tick of the number line; distractor cards stay off the line.
kindHints.barChart: Students draw a bar (or line) graph from the data; each category's value is checked. Put the data in the instruction or the image.
kindHints.gridDraw: The student draws rectangles that satisfy the rule on square (or dot) paper; position and orientation are free, every size that fits the rule is correct.
kindHints.balanceScale: Students balance the scale by putting weights on the two pans; equal pans are correct (several arrangements may be correct).
kindHints.clockSet: The student turns the hour and minute hands separately on an analog clock; correct when both are in place (at 3:45 the hour hand is between 3 and 4).
kindHints.crossword: Pick a cell on the grid, then enter the direction, clue and answer; the letters fill the cells. Students type the answers into the grid; each word is checked.
kindHints.wordSearch: Enter the words; the grid is built automatically. Students see either the words or the clues and find the words on the grid with a line.
kindHints.logicGrid: Students use the clues to put ✓ / ✗ in the grid; each row's answer in every category is checked. With two or more categories the book-style staircase grid is shown.

blanks.textHint: Example: The capital of France is [[Paris]]. Alternatives: [[twelve|12]].

shortAnswer.hint: Numeric answers become number boxes (3/4 equals 0.75).
shortAnswer.question: Question {{n}}
shortAnswer.cipherHint: Type the secret word and give each question its letter. The letter appears in the word when the student answers that question correctly.

table.hint: Answer cell: [[answer]]. A cell can mix text and a blank: [[5]] cm.
table.focusHint: Click a cell and press "Make blank": the whole cell becomes the answer; if you select part of the text, only that part. For several cells use "Select cells".
table.selectHint: Click cells or drag to select (Space on the keyboard), then "Make blank" / "Remove blank". Turn "Select cells" off to type.

wordPool.textHint: Example: Water freezes at [[0]] °C and boils at [[100]] °C. The same word may fill several blanks.

maze.doubleDiagonalHere: Two diagonal doors in this square; remove one.
maze.diagonalLocked: The other diagonal door of this square is open; remove it first.
maze.exitTitle: Exit name (the student sees it at the end of the path). Use Add level for a new statement.
maze.roomsHint: As in the game: type the door answer in the slot between rooms (empty = wall; one diagonal door per square of four). Pick the start with the walker and the finish with the flag; click the correct door in each room.
maze.treeHint: Type statements right into the tree; pick the correct branch under each. Flagged boxes are exits; use Add level for a new row of statements. The highlighted path is the correct route.
maze.boardHint: As in the game: finish on top, start at the bottom. The student climbs up; click the bulb on the correct box in each row.
maze.stonesHint: Stones appear in this order (bottom to top, two columns). Switch the stones the student must not step on to «Do not step»; at least one stone must stay «Step».

crossword.hint: Pick a cell on the grid, then type the direction, the question and the answer; the answer's letters are written into the cells. Add rows / columns on any side if you need room; empty edges are trimmed when saving, so students only see the area with words.
crossword.placed: All words were placed crossing each other.
crossword.unplaced: These words could not cross another word and were placed on their own row: {{list}}
crossword.extractHint: Add the puzzle image above and press "Read from image": Claude reads the grid, the word slots and the clues; you type the answers. Check and fix what was read; the same image is free the second time.
crossword.extractConfirm: The words in the form will be replaced by the ones read from the image.
crossword.extracted: {{n}} word slots read; type the answers and check the grid.
crossword.extractEmpty: No crossword grid could be read from the image.
crossword.extractFailed: The crossword could not be read from the image. Try again or type it in.
crossword.extractUnavailable: Claude is not available right now.
crossword.pickCell: Tap the cell where the word starts. Tapping the first cell of a word opens it for editing.
crossword.needAnswer: The answer needs at least 2 letters.
crossword.badChars: The answer may only contain letters and digits.
crossword.noRoomRight: The answer does not fit to the right; add a column or pick another cell.
crossword.noRoomDown: The answer does not fit downward; add a row or pick another cell.
crossword.letterConflict: The red cell already holds a different letter of another word.
crossword.sameDirTaken: Another word in the same direction uses these cells.

wordSearch.hint: Enter the words; the grid is built from them automatically and empty cells are filled with letters. Use "Shuffle" to place them again. Students see either the words or the clues in the list.
wordSearch.label: Clue

logicGrid.hint: This area is the student's screen. Write the clues, then fill in the answer table below as in the book (row group and categories in the header, each row's item and answers); options and the solution come from the table. Set the option order the student sees with the ‹ › and shuffle buttons in the grid header.
logicGrid.subject: Row {{n}}
logicGrid.rowOrderInfo: Categories whose options follow the row order: {{names}}. The correct answers line up on the diagonal; you can change the order with ‹ › or shuffle in the grid header.

regionPaint.hint: Choose the grid size and colours. Write each colour's target as in the book: fraction (2/5), decimal (0.35), percent (25%) or a square count. A colour with no target is a distractor (must stay unused). Optionally give the label shown on its palette button (e.g. "2/5").
regionPaint.hintPie: Choose the number of slices and the colours. Write each colour's target as in the book: fraction (1/4), decimal (0.25), percent (25%) or a slice count. A colour with no target is a distractor (must stay unused).
regionPaint.label: Label (optional)
regionPaint.cellsInvalid: not a whole number of squares
regionPaint.cellsPieInvalid: not a whole number of slices

numberLine.hint: Students place the cards on the ticks of a number line. Split the line into equal parts (ticks are numbered from 0 to the number of parts), label the ticks you want (e.g. 0 and 1, or "impossible", "even", "certain"). Enter each card's target tick; a card left empty is a distractor (it should stay off the line). For estimation use many parts + tolerance + "Hide ticks".
numberLine.hideTicks: Hide ticks (only labelled ones are drawn)

barChart.hint: Students draw the graph from the data. Set the vertical axis: the largest value, the interval of labelled lines and the smallest step students can set (e.g. 0–10, labels every 2, steps of 1). Enter each category's correct value; a category marked "Given" is already drawn for the student (complete-the-graph questions). Put the data table in the instruction or the image.
barChart.title: Graph title

gridDraw.hint: The student draws rectangles on the grid; checking uses the rule (area and/or perimeter in unit squares). With "all", every matching size must be drawn; otherwise one is enough. Also state the rule in the instruction (e.g. "Draw all rectangles with a perimeter of 14 cm").

balanceScale.hint: Weight values are visible to students (as in the book). Checking uses the rule: equal pan totals mean balance. An empty label shows value + unit; you can also write an expression (e.g. "(7+3)+2").
balanceScale.hideTilt: Keep the scale level until checked
balanceScale.label: Label (optional)
balanceScale.left: Given loads on the left pan
balanceScale.right: Given loads on the right pan

clockSet.hint: Clocks use a 12-hour dial (15:45 equals 3:45). A "pre-set" clock is shown already set and is not checked (e.g. the start time of a duration question). The time itself is not shown to the student; give it in the instruction.
clockSet.label: Label of clock {{n}} (optional)
